proceedings.supporting_quote: On 13 September 2016 the Aliens Office, the administrative body responsible for issuing visas (see paragraph 45 below), refused to grant “humanitarian visas” to the applicants
On 7 October 2016 the Aliens Appeals Board, acting under the extremely urgent procedure, ordered a stay of execution of the refusals by the Aliens Office
the Aliens Office issued new decisions, dated 10 October 2016, refusing to grant the visas
By a judgment of 14 October 2016 the Aliens Appeals Board, acting under the extremely urgent procedure, again ordered a stay of execution of the decision of 10 October 2016
On 17 October 2016 the Aliens Office again took decisions refusing to issue the visas
By a judgment of 20 October 2016 the Aliens Appeals Board... ordered a stay of execution of the refusal decisions of 17 October 2016

proceedings.deciding_body: Brussels French-language Court of First Instance
proceedings.supporting_quote: By an order of 25 October 2016... the acting president of the French-language TPI ordered the State, as an urgent measure, to comply with the Board’s judgment of 20 October 2016

proceedings.deciding_body: Brussels French-language Court of First Instance
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 7 November 2016 another judge acting as president of the French-language TPI declared their application admissible but unfounded
The applicants subsequently submitted such an application, which was rejected by the Belgian authorities in December 2016
On an appeal by the applicants, the Brussels Court of Appeal delivered a judgment on 7 December 2016 varying the order of 7 November 2016
the Belgian State... lodged a unilateral action to that effect with the President of the Brussels Dutch-speaking TPI on 13 December 2016, but was unsuccessful (order of the same date)
on an appeal by the Belgian State, the court of appeal varied the decision of the first-instance court in a judgment of 14 December 2016
On 6 March 2017 the Aliens Appeals Board... decided in consequence to lift the stay of execution

By a judgment of 24 March 2017 the Aliens Appeals Board dismissed the application to have the decisions set aside and ordered that the stay of execution in respect of the visa refusal decisions be lifted
the Belgian State sought to counter the execution of the above-cited decisions; it secured this aim through the court of appeal’s judgment of 30 June 2017

On 20 December 2017 the French-language enforcement judge, examining the action brought by the applicants on 15 December 2016, found that the case had become devoid of purpose following the Brussels Court of Appeal’s judgment of 30 June 2017
On 8 February 2018 the Conseil d’État dismissed an appeal on points of law by the applicants against the judgment of 6 March 2017
An administrative appeal on points of law lodged by the applicants against that judgment was dismissed by the Conseil d’État on 17 May 2018
On 27 February 2017 the Belgian State lodged an appeal on points of law against the court of appeal’s judgment of 7 December 2016. Those proceedings are currently pending.
On the same date the Belgian State brought proceedings against the applicants before the enforcement judge at the Brussels Dutch-language TPI
they brought proceedings before the administrative courts to challenge the refusal by the Aliens Office to issue them with visas

proceedings.deciding_body: Brussels French-language Court of First Instance
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 15 December 2016 the applicants brought an action against the Belgian State before the enforcement judge at the Brussels French-language TPI
